cascade.closed_form: 10 ** max(0, digits - 5) over the decimal digits of the reference; a reference of 0 yields 1
cascade.tail_bands: compares against 10**14 - 1 (assigns 10**9) and 10**15 - 1 (assigns 10**10 - 1, incremented to 10**10), then against 10**16, 10**17, 10**18 (assigning 10**11 - 1, 10**12 - 1, 10**13 - 1, each incremented), then against 10**19: below it a cmovb loads 10**14 - 1 (incremented to 10**14), at or above it the 10**15 - 1 value stands (incremented to 10**15)

not_claimed: what the object, its table, or its fields denote beyond the pinned offsets and reads
what the table byte encodes beyond its pinned range 0..6 and the 10 ** (6 - byte) contribution
what any caller does with the returned power of ten

behaviour on a null object pointer or a table pointer that does not cover the remainder's entry (the binary faults on the same reads; the model takes the byte through a lookup and does not invent table contents)
the panic runtime past the payload builder at 0x1680e80 (shipped whole; its own callee is not modelled)
caller semantics beyond the sites, FDE ranges, and pinned register moves in callers.tsv

result.combine: cmp + cmovb at 0x5a012df..0x5a012e2 keeps the smaller of the cascade power (rcx) and the table power (rdx)

routine.first_instruction: push %rax (no endbr64; the routine is reached only by direct calls)
routine.returns: one power of ten in rax, through the single ret at 0x5a012ea

sub_overflow_exit.condition: the table byte is 7 or more
sub_overflow_exit.passed_length_rule: the shim passes the pre-encoded length 2 * 33 + 1 = 67 and calls the payload builder at 0x1680e80 through the slot at 0x64df6b8 directly

unwrap_exit.condition: quotient != *(object +0x50), or remainder >= *(object +0x10); both failures converge on this exit and the table is not read
unwrap_exit.forwarder: 0x1680e60, reached through the slot at 0x64df730; it rewrites the message length len -> 2 * len + 1 and calls the payload builder at 0x1680e80 through the slot at 0x64df6b8
